n: Blessed is the person who pays attention to the weak and helps them; God will rescue that person in his own trouble. Compassion is returned.

f.g: Pays thoughtful attention to, acts wisely toward.

n: God will protect such a person, keep him alive, and bless him, never handing him over to his enemies.
When this person is sick in bed, God will sustain him and tend to him like a caregiver changing his bed.

f.g: Turn or change his bed — care for him through his illness.

n: Now David speaks from his own sickbed, asking for healing of his soul and confessing his sin.
His enemies speak cruelly: “When will he die and be forgotten?”
A visitor comes pretending sympathy, but collects gossip to spread once he leaves.
Everyone who hates him whispers together and plans the worst for him.
They say a deadly disease has gripped him: “He’s down and won’t get up again.”

f.g: Literally “a thing of Belial” — something wicked or deadly.

n: Worst of all, a close friend who shared his table turned against him. Jesus quoted this verse about Judas, who ate with him and then betrayed him.

f.w: lifted up his heel against me
f.g: An image of kicking or turning on someone — treacherous betrayal.
Literally “man of my peace” — a trusted companion.

n: David asks God to raise him up so he can set things right with his enemies. As king, restoring justice was his duty.

f.g: Repay, give back what is due.

n: Proof of God’s favor: his enemy hasn’t been allowed to shout in victory over him.
God supports David because of his integrity and places him in his presence forever — the greatest of blessings.

f.w: settest me before thy face for ever

n: This doxology closes the first of the five “books” of the Psalms (Psalms 1–41). Each book ends with a burst of praise like this one.

f.g: “So be it” — a word of firm agreement.
